atlas-fr.0274: For social security, a birth certificate in Italian, English, German, Spanish and several other languages needs no translation; in other languages it needs a sworn translator.
atlas-fr.0275: Get the long-stay visa (VLS-TS, type D) in your country of residence before you travel, through Campus France and France-Visas for students: entering visa-free, you cannot apply for a student or work permit in France.
atlas-fr.0276: What offices ask for is proof of address (justificatif de domicile): a lease or a utility bill in your name. High-street banks want it before opening an account.
atlas-fr.0277: No residence card is needed. After 3 months your right to stay rests on working, or studying with health insurance and enough money, or having enough money and insurance: keep proof of which applies.
atlas-fr.0278: Validate your long-stay visa online within 3 months of arriving: the fee is €100, and the validated visa is your residence permit for its first year.
atlas-fr.0279: If you have never filed in France, ask your local public finance centre for a tax number with form Cerfa 2043, your passport and proof of address.
atlas-fr.0280: File a tax return every spring, even with no income: without the tax notice, the family benefits office (CAF) stops housing aid.
atlas-fr.0281: A student who does not work is covered by their European Health Insurance Card; any job or paid internship in France means registering with the health insurance fund (CPAM).
atlas-fr.0282: Students register free at etudiant-etranger.ameli.fr: you get a provisional number at once, then the permanent social security number and the Carte Vitale, typically after 6 to 12 months. Until then, send the doctor’s paper claim form to the fund for refunds.
atlas-fr.0283: Public insurance refunds 70% of the standard €30 GP fee, less a €2 flat charge, and nothing above it: a top-up policy (mutuelle) is strongly advised.
atlas-fr.0284: An online bank with a French IBAN opens at once. If a high-street bank refuses you in writing, the Banque de France names a bank within 1 working day, which must open a free basic account within 3 working days.
atlas-fr.0285: If the basis of your stay ends, for instance studies finish without a job, and you rely on welfare, the prefecture can order you to leave.
atlas-fr.0286: Apply to renew between 4 and 2 months before your permit expires; outside that window there is a €180 penalty.
atlas-fr.0287: A first-application receipt does not let you leave and come back. A renewal receipt with your expired card lets you travel in Schengen, but avoid flights out of Schengen or with stopovers until you have the new card: airlines often refuse paper receipts.
atlas-fr.0288: A receipt for a first application does not let you leave and re-enter France; even a renewal receipt, a plain PDF, is often refused by airlines on flights outside Schengen or with a stopover. Avoid such trips until you hold the plastic card.
atlas-fr.0289: If the reason for your stay ends (studies over, no job) and you rely on social benefits, the prefecture can order you to leave France.
atlas-fr.0290: File a tax return every spring, even with no income: without the tax notice you lose your housing benefit from the CAF.
atlas-fr.0291: Prefecture appointments sold by bots and middlemen are risky and can be cancelled; if you cannot get one, a court can order the prefecture to give you one.
atlas-fr.0292: Pay nothing for a flat before visiting it and signing the lease; the free state guarantee VISALE covers tenants aged 18 to 30.
atlas-fr.0293: Airlines and foreign police often refuse the PDF renewal receipt at the gate, especially on flights with a stopover.
atlas-fr.0294: Busy prefectures (Paris area, Lyon, Marseille) take 6 to 10 months to renew a card, and some backdate the new card, shortening it.
atlas-fr.0295: Most private landlords and agencies refuse the VISALE guarantee, although student residences accept it.
atlas-fr.0296: The students’ proof of funds now follows the minimum wage: it will rise with the next increase, due on 1 January 2027.
atlas-fr.0297: Some consulates want an irrevocable transfer certificate (AVI) and reject those from unlicensed online providers; no official list of accepted providers was found.
